description: Issue summary: Customer running Redwood Private (VPC deployment) reported intermittent timeouts when the agent attempts to download model shards during scale-up. Impact: model downloads fail ~20-40% of the time causing model pull timeouts and repeated retries; application-level requests see increased cold-start latency and some timeouts. Environment: Private deployment in Acme Health VPC, prod, us-west-2. Deployed Redwood agent v2.8.1 with serving runtime pinned to v1.14. Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger a scale-up on a new node in the VPC (deploy new serving instance). 2) Observe agent attempting parallel downloads of model shards from Redwood store. 3) Note intermittent TLS connection failures and incomplete downloads. Observed behavior: TLS sessions sometimes fail during handshake or mid-transfer; tcp retransmits and RSTs seen for high-numbered source ports. Expected behavior: model shard downloads should complete reliably over outbound HTTPS without connection resets. Business impact: customer-facing features degrade; Acme Health is an enterprise-regulated customer on a private deployment contract, urgent for uptime and SLA compliance.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a new serving instance in the customer's private deployment in us-west-2. 2) Force a cold-start (ensure no cached KV prefixes). 3) Watch agent logs for model pull events. 4) Note any failed shard download attempts or TLS errors in logs. Observed on ~4 out of 10 cold starts during the incident window.

comments: 2026-03-12 09:30 - Support (Priya Shah): Initial report received from Acme Health. Assigned to networking oncall. Customer reports intermittent model download failures and higher cold-start times. Provided temporary guidance to increase retry limits.

2026-03-12 10:05 - Networking Oncall (Ethan Morales): Started packet captures and asked customer to run ephemeral port connectivity test (connectivity check script provided). Noted RSTs to high source ports in pcap. Suspecting corporate FW restricting ephemeral port ranges for outbound connections or asymmetric firewall behavior.

2026-03-12 12:18 - Acme Health (Customer): Sent firewall team logs. They confirmed a corporate egress policy that blocks outbound connections from ephemeral source ports above 50000 as a mitigant for a legacy app. Customer is willing to relax rule for Redwood endpoints.

2026-03-12 15:40 - Security (R&ED) (A. Lopez): Confirmed model pull implementation uses concurrent outbound HTTPS connections; each uses an ephemeral source port per connection. If outbound ephemeral ports are filtered or subject to sticky NAT translation which rewrites source ports beyond limits, TLS handshakes can fail. Recommended allowlist of ephemeral port range and to avoid stateful firewall timeouts on short-lived connections.

2026-03-13 08:22 - Support (Priya Shah): Escalated to customer success and scheduled a maintenance window with Acme Health for the firewall change. Provided temporary engineering workaround: switch agent to single-connection fallback in agent v2.8.2 (patch), but customer preferred firewall change instead.

2026-03-14 07:10 - Acme Health (Customer): Firewall team applied rule change to allow outbound ephemeral ports 32768-61000 to hosts in the subnet and removed aggressive RST injection. Support validated model pulls after change; cold-start time returned to baseline. Customer confirmed impact resolved.
2026-03-14 09:05 - Support (Ethan Morales): Marking resolved. Follow-up runbook updates created and scheduled for rollout to onboarding docs.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: corporate egress firewall was rejecting/blackholing outbound TCP flows originating from high ephemeral source ports used by the agent's concurrent connections. Verified via pcap: immediate RSTs to client source ports >50000, retransmits and mid-transfer EOFs in TLS. Packet captures from inside VPC matched RSTs originating from corporate FW appliance (hash/sig in tcpdump), and firewall logs confirmed policy. Reproduction: running provided ephemeral-port-check.sh from customer instance produced failures when source port >50000. Engineering considered a protocol change (multiplex/download-over-single-connection) but judged that allowing ephemeral port range is correct fix for general networking interoperability. Customer applied firewall rule to allow ephemeral range 32768-61000 for relevant subnets and stopped injecting RSTs. Verified by repeated cold-starts and model pull logs.
resolution: Root cause: corporate egress firewall aggressively blocked/terminated outbound TCP flows using high ephemeral source ports causing TLS handshakes and model shard downloads to fail intermittently. Fix: Acme Health firewall team relaxed egress policy to allow ephemeral source ports 32768-61000 for the Redwood agent subnets and removed RST injection. Result: model pulls became stable and cold-start latencies returned to normal. Workaround applied earlier: agent patch v2.8.2 introduced single-connection fallback for environments that cannot change firewall rules; recommended but customer chose firewall update. Follow-up actions: 1) Add ephemeral port connectivity check to Private onboarding checklist. 2) Update runbook "private-deploy-network-checks" with ephemeral port guidance and sample firewall rules. 3) Consider adding a built-in network diagnostic in the agent that alerts when high-rate connection resets are observed.
